correctness.rationale: All colour classes j>=2 are singletons at diameter at most two; the colour-1 class lies in exactly one independent part. A block without high-colour vertices is broadcast dominating precisely when it is that entire part. This establishes the maximum class capacity, Stirling partition count, falling-factorial injection enumeration, exact three-phase palette minimum, and all equality cases without extrapolation. Separate exhaustive distance-and-partition enumeration for 116 graph/palette cases (67,470 feasible colourings) and 96 optimality cases agrees.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete, natural two-parameter census of a newly studied distance-packing/broadcast-partition invariant across every labelled complete multipartite graph. It counts both colourings and witness partitions, classifies every optimal colouring, and exhibits part-size-gap jumps invisible from ordinary packing chromatic number. Example: K_{3,3} has chromatic spectrum (4,4,4,4,6,7), with a sharp two-unit transition. The full normalised counts are precise data for random coloured broadcasts and robustness/uniqueness questions, not just a cosmetic restatement of a previously known scalar.
